test: history return retains card input and a cached pagehide does not consume final cleanup

firstFullRun.failedAssertion: The first hover after native history return did not retain data-tracking=true. Later lifecycle assertions were not reached.

observations: The first-full-run trace shows the hover target shifting vertically by 171px while the action was in progress.
In the instrumented reproduction the returned document was visible, motion was enabled and fine-pointer media matched.
A real pointermove set tracking to true. Continuing scroll then cleared tracking through the existing scroll-reset handler and moved the card away from the pointer.
The reproduced scroll position progressed from 145px to 437px and finally 515px. After scrolling settled, a new real pointer input inside the card immediately restored tracking.
investigation.conclusion: The test raced with navigation/scroll restoration. Evidence did not show a lost listener or broken cached-page cleanup. Resetting pointer coordinates after scrolling remains intended product behavior.

details: Wait for loaded fonts, finite document animations to stop and four successive animation-frame samples of stable scroll and card geometry.
Move the pointer outside, then send explicit fresh positions inside the real card.
Retain native link navigation and history return, tracking assertions, both injected pagehide lifecycle branches and cleanup assertions.
Additionally verify actual computed SVG horizontal displacement changes after the second pointer position.

verification.unchangedResultsReused: The first full run's other 100 passing cases remain applicable because product sources did not change. This is not a claim that a second complete 101-case suite was run.

evidenceBoundary: Raw traces and instrumented machine output remain in private verification storage. This report includes only local browser observations and test results; no real-device or deployment claim is made.
